newsitem.title: LEBANON: Saudi minister tells Israel to revive peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi minister tells Israel to revive peace talks.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Foreign Minister Prince Saud al-Faisal on Friday urged Israel to stick to the principle of land-for-peace to break the deadlock in the peace process.

"Arab and international efforts should concentrate on returning to the...land-for-peace formula and the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people. This is the only way to push all other matters such as multilateral negotiation," he said on an official visit to Beirut before departing.
"Arab steadfastness and an altered Israeli position is the only thing that can change this (stalled peace process)," he told reporters.
Saudi Crown Prince Abdullah arrived in Beirut on Thursday accompanied by Prince Saud and other officials in the first visit by a senior Saudi official in nearly two decades.
Arab states have slammed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for refusing to swap occupied Arab land for peace -- the formula on which the Arab Israeli peace negotiations were based.
Crown Prince Abdullah stressed his support in seeking the removal of Israeli forces from south Lebanon.
Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter and producer, is an influential Middle East player and a key ally of the United States.

Lebanon coordinates its peace moves with Damascus. Syrian-Israeli and Lebanese-Israeli peace talks have been stalled over Israel's refusal to withdraw from the occupied Syrian Golan heights and south Lebanon.
Lebanese newspapers welcomed Prince Abdullah's visit. "Abdullah's tour is intended to restore Arab solidarity and unified Arab action," said a columnist in the an-Nahar newspaper.
